blockers.governingConflict: At the pinned control-protocol-contract.v2 bytes, handshake.ownVersionSurface says controlProtocolMajor is its own surface, NEVER shared with core, component, or either provider protocol; only major 1 exists. downgradeAndRefusalRules says majors are the only compatibility unit, and compatibilityMatrixRow says no cross-major window exists before a second major. Thus the surviving ordinary reading of 'each at N and N+1' still demands a nonexistent control major 2 and couples three independent version axes. Reading 'each' as excluding control leaves that exclusion unstated.

Live file 08 agrees: DR-G18 owns rollback/generation recovery; DR-G16 owns aggregate release selection and signed lane closure; DR-G21 owns crash/panic/timeout/resource/malformed/EOF/process-tree failure containment.

Route AL-1/AL-2/AL-5 selection and qualification evidence to a reviewed owning gate such as DR-G16 only to the extent its accepted contract covers them; otherwise keep that remainder explicitly at DR-127 pending a reviewed gate/owner addition. Pin the consumed contract/decision and claim no QUALIFIED or SATISFIED standing.

blockers.title: Independent version labels still do not prove independent publication or promotion
blockers.subjectEvidence: releaseIdentities forbids shared-version equality, a required same-version train, and bundle existence as eligibility/qualification/promotion predicates. It does not prohibit a shared promotion transaction or train when core and component retain different version axes. AL-1/AL-2 observe only post-publication selectability with the running counterpart identity unchanged. requiredRecords contains release digests, selection outcomes, rollback/coexistence, and bundle/non-bundle qualification records, but no before/after publication set, promotion decision, or proof that one release became available while no counterpart release was co-promoted. releaseIdentities.proof incorrectly treats a later compatible unequal-version non-bundle selection as proof of the promotion rule.
blockers.counterexample: Assign core versions C10/C11 and component versions P37/P38, independently and never equal. Require every C and P release to enter availability together under one non-bundle train ticket, but after joint promotion allow C10+P38 and C11+P37 selection, independent rollback, coexistence, and every required record. No equality or bundle predicate exists, so the authored lockstepFail text and AL-1..AL-5 records pass, yet neither side can publish or promote without the other.
blockers.governingConflict: At the pinned file-02 bytes, independent releases select independently qualified compatible bytes; the blueprint is not merely independently numbered compatibility after a coordinated release act. Codex v1's required repair expressly called for independent publication/promotion and a pass/fail record distinguishing a jointly promoted train. v2 supplies identities and post-promotion selection records but omits both remaining elements while honestyRepairsFromV1 says the finding is repaired in full.
blockers.requiredRepair: Add explicit independent-release transitions and records: for AL-1, show a component release becomes admitted/qualifiable/promotable while the core publication set and identity remain unchanged; for AL-2, the reciprocal. Record the promotion/eligibility decision inputs and prove no shared train ticket, synchronized availability act, version equality, or bundle predicate is required. Keep post-publication skew selection as a separate compatibility proof rather than treating it as proof of independent promotion.
